messages:
maya: ran a quick multi-region latency + throughput sweep for llama3-small int8 on h100 + a100 across us-east / us-west / eu-west. quick summary: p50s tight, eu-west p95 is outlier. raw CSV: https://console.redwood.ai/bench/zz-301
anika: paste the exact bench command and config (batch, seq, concurrency, warmup, route policy)
maya: test cmd:
```
rb-bench --model llama3-small --quant int8 --hw h100,a100 --regions us-east,us-west,eu-west --batch 8 --seq 512 --concurrency 60 --duration 5m --warmup 1m
```
maya: numbers (h100): us-east p50=32ms p95=78ms throughput≈1150 tok/s; eu-west p50=38ms p95=165ms throughput≈1110 tok/s. a100 shows same pattern but p95s larger variance.
tom: that eu-west p95 x2 suggests network/edge hop queuing, not core kernel perf. did you pin routing or use smart-route?
maya: default smart-route. when I forced region header (route -> eu-west) p95 dropped to ~98ms, so routing path affects tails.
raz: checked proxies for the window — eu-west egress hit edge-proxy-7 which had intermittent 60–120ms queue spikes (seen in req queue length and egress latency). opened INC-2029 to track proxy fanout imbalance.
liam: mitigation options: 1) temp prefer local-pop routing for the canary (safe, quick), 2) kernel fallback for small-batch tails (fast-gemm quant path) — may cost a few % throughput but helps p95, 3) increase warmup tokens for eu-west shards to reduce cold-tail hits.
maya: also observed int8 on a100 amplifies jitter for small-batch sequence profiles — quant+kernels interplay needs a sweep.
infra-bot: canary update applied: routing.policy=local_pop_preference -> eu-west for 30m. see https://console.redwood.ai/canary/INC-2029
anika: please re-run bench with `--route-policy local_pop_preference` and `--warmup 2m` and post CSVs. include both h100 and a100 runs.
maya: re-ran h100 with local_pop + 2m warmup: eu-west p50=36ms p95=92ms, throughput ~1115 tok/s (≈ -3% vs baseline). I'll upload CSVs and a short heatmap slide in the channel. a100 sweep queued.
liam: for capacity planning assume you need ~1.3x capacity to hit same p95 SLA if you keep default routing. with local-pop_preference that drops to ~1.1x for seq512/batch8. document these multipliers in Sizing doc.
raz: continuing proxy remediation work, monitoring for regressions. INC-2029 tracking all follow-ups.
maya: action items:
- @raz continue proxy fix + post remediation ETA (INC-2029)
- @anika & @maya run full h100/a100 int8 sweeps with `--route-policy local_pop_preference` and `--warmup 2m`, upload CSVs and raw logs
- @liam quantify kernel-fallback cost vs p95 improvement and suggest thresholds (batch/seq/concurrency)
- ops: consider a short-term routing policy toggle for high-p50/p95 customers in eu-west

maya: will post CSV links and 2-slide summary in ~2h :thumbsup:
